ai_show_review.summary: High‑octane set with soaring Dark Star and fierce The Eleven
ai_show_review.blurb: The show delivers relentless high energy, highlighted by an expansive Dark Star, a ferocious The Eleven, and a magical Turn On Your Lovelight. Jerry’s guitar soars while Phil drives the low end with front‑and‑center bass, and Pigpen adds gritty organ and vocal fire. A seamless Caution → Feedback transition caps the set with raw intensity.
ai_show_review.review: On October 20, 1968 at Berkeley’s Greek Theatre the Dead turned in a concise yet blistering performance that still feels fresh decades later. The first song, Good Morning Little School Girl, sets a gritty tone before Pigpen lifts the crowd with Turn On Your Lovelight, then launches into an otherworldly Dark Star where Jerry’s hypnotic leads and Phil’s “nasty” bass intertwine. A cooking Saint Stephen segues straight into the relentless meter‑shifting The Eleven, which rockets into Caution (Do Not Stop On Tracks) and bursts out into Feedback for a high‑octane finish. Throughout, Pigpen’s organ and vocal grit keep the sound grounded while Mickey and Bill hold down a tight dual‑drum groove that never overshadows the improvisational fireworks.

best_recording.reason: Crystal‑clear soundboard capture with every instrument audible and minimal tape noise, delivering the most faithful listening experience of this high‑energy show.

key_highlights: Soaring Dark Star with hypnotic guitar and front‑and‑center bass.
Ferocious The Eleven that drives the set into overdrive.
Magical Turn On Your Lovelight that segues smoothly into Dark Star.
Seamless Caution → Feedback transition that caps a relentless first set.

band_performance.Jerry: His guitar is hypnotic and flowing, delivering amazing fills on Dark Star and a cooking solo on Saint Stephen; overall the lead work is described as "cooking" and soaring.
band_performance.Phil: Bass sits front‑and‑center, described as "nasty" on School Girl and booming throughout; delivers an extended solo that fans highlight as powerful and in charge.
band_performance.Bob: Pigpen’s organ work and vocals are tip‑top and rocking, adding vital grit to the performance.
